findings.evidence: "The same formula is quoted verbatim in §4.3, and the ~1.08 s prefill residual used in §2.3 is the two-term part of it (retrieval + prefill) with no allowance for the other terms."
findings.issue: Confusing referent: 1.08 s is the prefill term only (1.2 s − 0.12 s retrieval), not the 'two-term part' (retrieval + prefill). The sentence reads as if 1.08 s equals retrieval + prefill, which contradicts §2.3 and Table 4-2. §4.3 and Table 4-2 correctly state 1.08 s is the prefill residual; only this Preface-internal restatement mangles it.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite to: 'the ~1.08 s prefill residual used in §2.3 is the prefill term of that two-term budget (retrieval + prefill), with no allowance for the other terms.'

findings.evidence: "The required rate against the ~1.08 s two-term prefill residual (TTFT SLO minus retrieval time — an upper cap, not a deployable prefill target; see Ch 4, Table 4-2)"
findings.issue: Ch 2 §2.3 refers to the 1.2 s value as 'TTFT SLO', but Ch 4 §4.3 explicitly states 'The 1.2 s and ~25 ms values are design budgets, not the pass/fail SLO thresholds. Pass/fail on a measured distribution is judged against the p95 ceilings (TTFT ≤ 2 s, TPOT ≤ 35 ms)'. The book holds this distinction sharply elsewhere (e.g. Ch 4 Table 4-1 'Latency' row: 'TTFT budget 1.2 s … p95 ceiling ≤ 2 s'); Ch 2 §2.3 is the one place that calls 1.2 s an SLO. The terminology slip directly contradicts the canonical Latency dimension definition.
findings.fix_instruction: Change 'TTFT SLO' to 'TTFT budget' on page 30 to match Ch 4's explicit design-budget-vs-SLO distinction.

findings.chapter: Ch. 2 — What Actually Happens During Inference
findings.evidence: §2.5 Common Mistakes: "Cross-technology numbers follow the same rule — name the SKU, not the memory class: the H200 (HBM3e successor to the H100) is 4.8 TB/s, B200-class HBM3e is ~8 TB/s, and AMD MI300X is ~5.3 TB/s [1P][FACT] — vendor-published specifications as of the 2026-08-30 cutoff; verify against the specific generation in use."
findings.issue: Three vendor hardware constants carry the [1P][FACT] pair, but no first-party source is named for any of them ("vendor-published specifications" is generic). The book's own evidence discipline requires a named first-party source for [1P] — compare Table 4-2's rows "[1P][FACT] NVIDIA H100 SXM5 datasheet (80 GB HBM3)" and "[1P][FACT] NVIDIA H100 SXM5 datasheet (1,979 TFLOPS with sparsity ÷ 2)", and the Preface's "[1P] — first-party: the model vendor's own spec". These three figures are load-bearing in the surrounding argument that "The comparison to the 5.6 TB/s decode demand shifts the GPU count equation" (Ch. 2 §2.7), so their provenance must be checkable.
findings.fix_instruction: Name the specific datasheet (or model card) behind each constant, e.g. "NVIDIA H200 SXM datasheet (HBM3e, 4.8 TB/s)", "NVIDIA B200 datasheet", "AMD Instinct MI300X datasheet", each with the access date, consistent with the Table 4-2 style; or downgrade the labels to [2°][DERIVED] if the figures are carried from a secondary summary.

findings.chapter: Ch. 2 — What Actually Happens During Inference
findings.evidence: §2.5 Common Mistakes: "H100 3.35 TB/s HBM3 is the theoretical peak; actual sustained bandwidth for weight-read kernels may be 60–80% of peak [HYPOTHESIS] — a rule of thumb, not measured or cited here."  The book's rule, Preface PDF p. 20 (book p. xvi): "Every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair (e.g. [1P][DERIVED]); Axis 3, measurement status, rides along where a claim's status is known."
findings.issue: A quantitative performance ratio (60–80% of peak) is tagged with Axis 2 only ([HYPOTHESIS]), with no Axis-1 provenance, violating the book's own two-axis label-pair rule for load-bearing quantitative claims. The same chapter applies the rule correctly elsewhere (e.g. "[canonical scenario][DERIVED]", "[1P][FACT]"), and the Preface states: "A label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes." The figure is also reused as an analytical input in the same paragraph ("the same shard takes ~8.7–6.5 ms", PDF p. 54), so it carries downstream weight.
findings.fix_instruction: Give the 60–80% figure a full pair — e.g. [2°][HYPOTHESIS] if it comes from an industry rule of thumb, or [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] if it is the book's own planning assumption — and add the Axis-3 status (MEASURED/UNMEASURED). If no provenance exists, remove the numeric range and state the qualitative point only.
